cards.myth: Addiction is only a lack of willpower.
cards.fact: Addiction involves changes in brain circuits for reward, stress, and self-control. Support and treatment matter — it is not simply a character flaw.

cards.myth: People have to hit rock bottom before they can get help.
cards.fact: Earlier support often works better. You do not need to wait for a crisis to learn, ask questions, or seek care.

cards.myth: Digital or behavioral addictions are not real because there is no substance.
cards.fact: Compulsive behaviors can still reinforce reward pathways and disrupt sleep, school, work, and relationships — even without a chemical.

cards.myth: If someone relapses, treatment failed and they should give up.
cards.fact: Recovery is often non-linear. Relapse can be a signal to adjust support, not proof that change is impossible.
Addiction can involve alcohol, nicotine, prescription medicines, gambling, and other behaviors — patterns of harm matter more than labels.

cards.myth: Talking about addiction with teens only encourages it.
cards.fact: Clear, calm, accurate information reduces stigma and helps people spot risk earlier. Silence often leaves myths unchallenged.
